title: dfilter: Add max() and min() functions
description:
Changes the function calling convention to pass the first register
number plus the number of registers after that sequentially. This
allows function with any number of arguments. Functions can still
only return one value.

Adds max() and min() function to select the maximum/minimum value
from any number of arguments, all of the same type. The functions
accept literals too. The return type is the same as the first argument
(cannot be a literal).

notes.body:
Testing, this does what I would want and expect with fields that occur more than once in a packet, say `tls.record.length`. It adds some interesting and sometimes quite useful filter options, and provides a number of ways to get a generic "all" functionality.

Do you think that the documentation should explicitly mention that this is useful for fields that occur more than once, and/or give examples of such?

I'm not sure how people expect byte comparisons of different lengths to compare; looks like right now length is used and it's not a lexicographical sort.

You mean bytes or protocols? They're different (and almost certainly they shouldn't be).

Protocols FTs are just weird. Bytes uses a lexicographical sort. If not that is a bug.

Look at the first frame in this file:
[git_smart.pcapng](/uploads/74f09f92317770ca670b36c5a74b19d0/git_smart.pcapng)

There are two TLS app data fields:
`ed54360056c2f199a07608201aad41cbab755eb60a384f4224952eeec1f31ccc`

and

`122b1838f7c3efa7d38ba4c04ec73c82b2738b63f0507dbb436d0a770d1787782b964c21c8302afc2a77d72ab15d7c5adc81628b22fac8ec37757ca4dc6e7911`

`tls.app_data == ed:54:36:00:56:c2:f1:99:a0:76:08:20:1a:ad:41:cb:ab:75:5e:b6:0a:38:4f:42:24:95:2e:ee:c1:f3:1c:cc` - matches

`min(tls.app_data) == ed:54:36:00:56:c2:f1:99:a0:76:08:20:1a:ad:41:cb:ab:75:5e:b6:0a:38:4f:42:24:95:2e:ee:c1:f3:1c:cc` - matches

`max(tls.app_data) == ed:54:36:00:56:c2:f1:99:a0:76:08:20:1a:ad:41:cb:ab:75:5e:b6:0a:38:4f:42:24:95:2e:ee:c1:f3:1c:cc` - does not match.

So the shorter field apparently sorts before the longer one, even though `ed` sorts after `12`. Have to do some more testing to be sure, but it looks like a shortlex ordering, not the normal dictionary lexicographical. I'm not sure what people expect.

You're right, it's not lexicographical, that was my mistake, it's a different sort (but it's totally ordered). The sort for max() and min() is the same as < or >, as you'd expect. I don't think that has been changed recently (but I will verify that).
I don't think it changed recently after testing some more. I was a little surprised with the comparison behavior of bytes when testing this change, but it's unrelated.

> Do you think that the documentation should explicitly mention that this is useful for fields that occur more than once, and/or give examples of such?

I don't understand what could be confusing or surprising about that to a user but sure, why not.

commits_data.title: dfilter: Allow function arguments to be non-existent.
commits_data.message:
dfilter: Allow function arguments to be non-existent.

Instead of not calling the function if an argument is non-existent
(read tree fails), call the function and let the function handle
the condition.
